verdict.rationale: Azure ships its own local emulators, Azurite for Storage and the Cosmos DB emulator, which give real isolated test environments away from production data. These are service-scoped, though: there is no platform-wide sandbox, the Learn training sandbox is retired, REST Try It runs against the caller's real subscription, and the free account is credits on production. Missing for 10: a platform-wide hosted or API sandbox covering services beyond Storage/Cosmos DB, a non-production Try It target, and hands-on corroboration of emulator fidelity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: The Azurite open-source emulator provides a free local environment for testing your Azure storage applications
provides a local environment that emulates the Azure Cosmos DB service
Sandboxes are no longer available. To complete exercises in training modules, you'll need access to an Azure subscription.
Executing Try It requires Microsoft sign-in and runs against the caller's real subscription at management.azure.com.
